pass_a_gloss:
Veins and arteries, marrow not yet formed, membranes being woven, hairs being straightened. The body was being constructed slowly by the word of the limbs. Just as a horse is formed from a composite, so the dead man, awakened by the voice of the Lord, was called, formed, and appeared from the tomb. 'Lazarus, come out.' Before saying 'arise', he commands the exit. The one lying down is still being hastened to run. 'First, Lord, raise him, and then, having arisen, command him to run.' Why do you proclaim the exit to the one lying down before the resurrection? - 'Yes, to the one lying down', he says, 'I command the run, so that I may not, having been occupied with the dead for two things, delay the exit. I say to him: 'Come out', so that he may run more quickly, having taken one deadline for both resurrection and run.' Immediately, Lazarus, as if a guardian rather than a dead man, jumped out of the tomb. Hades below, as it seems, gave back the dead man and cried out: 'Who is this who, with his voice, awakens the dead from their tombs as if from sleep? Who is this who loosens the old laws of the dead? Who is this who provokes me to raise my dead? Who is this who proclaims a return to the dead? Who is this who trains the buried to run back to life? Who is this who so easily releases my prisoners? Who is this who takes away all my dead to a dance? My scepter of tyranny over humans is being taken away, as I see. My prison of death is rotten. Elijah took one of my dead away for the sake of a woman. After Elijah, Elisha, a double snatcher of my dead, came.

Now this one is more bitter than the dead to me, having campaigned as a helper, calling the dead who have been buried as if they were living, and I am in danger of not being in control even of the dead who have not been buried; for I have been robbed of a dead person whom I had buried; the four-day-old corpse triumphs over me, with the funeral clothes dancing together with the living; I will be trampled afterwards, with the swaddling clothes of the dead person who has escaped beside me; for who will frighten me, who have been conquered by the dead person and have become like a guardian of the dead; for Lazarus is a kind of deposit of the tomb, like gold given with seals; having been bound with bands, he was placed with the tomb, and with the same bonds, he was given back to life; for the Jewish crowd was unbelieving and doubtful towards the great wonder-working, I would say about Lazarus even now…
pass_b_english: The formation of the body is a complex process, involving the development of veins and arteries, as well as the creation of marrow, membranes, and hairs.
The body is constructed slowly, with each limb being formed by the power of the word.
Just as a horse is formed from various components, the dead man, awakened by the voice of the master, is called, formed, and appears from the tomb.
The command to Lazarus is clear: 'Lazarus, come out' (John 11:43).
Before saying 'arise', he commands the exit.
First, Lord, raise him, and then, having arisen, command him to run.
The one lying down is still being hastened to run, a remarkable transformation.
Why do you proclaim the exit to the one lying down before the resurrection?

He says, 'Yes, to the one lying down, I command the run, so that I may not, having been occupied with the dead for two things, delay the exit. I say to him: 'Come out', so that he may run more quickly, having taken one deadline for both resurrection and run.'
Immediately, Lazarus jumps out of the tomb, as if he were a guardian rather than a dead man.
Hades below, as it seems, gives back the dead man and cries out in response.
Hades asks who this is who, with his voice, awakens the dead from their tombs as if from sleep.
Hades asks who loosens the old laws of the dead.
Hades is provoked to raise his dead.
Hades asks who proclaims a return to the dead.
Hades sees his scepter of tyranny over humans being taken away, as he sees.
Hades acknowledges that his prison of death is rotten.
Hades recalls that Elijah took one of his dead away for the sake of a woman (1 Kings 17:22-24).
Hades notes that after Elijah, Elisha came and also snatched away some of his dead (2 Kings 4:32-37).
Hades finds that this one is more bitter to him than the dead, having campaigned as a helper, calling the dead who have been buried as if they were living.
Hades has been robbed of a dead person whom he had buried.
The four-day-old body triumphs over Hades, with the funeral clothes dancing together with the living.
Hades fears that he will be trampled afterwards, with the swaddling clothes of the dead person who has escaped beside him.
Hades wonders who will frighten him, now that he has been conquered by the dead person and has become like a guardian of the dead.
Hades sees Lazarus as a kind of deposit of the tomb, like gold given with seals.
Lazarus was bound with bands and placed with the tomb, but with the same bonds, he was given back to life.
